references.text: Moses warns the people of Israel against tempting the Lord, as they did at Massah.
Moses reminds the people how they provoked the Lord's anger at Massah and Meribah.
Moses' blessing over the tribe of Levi mentions the testing at Massah and the strife at Meribah.
The water of Meribah is mentioned again where the children of Israel quarreled with the Lord.
The psalm refers to the testing at the waters of Meribah.
A warning against hardening your heart as at Meribah and Massah, when your ancestors tempted God.
The psalm describes how the people provoked God's anger at the waters of Meribah.
Hebrews quotes Psalm 95 and warns against hardening your hearts as during the testing in the wilderness.
Paul warns against tempting Christ, as some of the Israelites did in the wilderness.
A theological contrast where the people test God in Exodus, while God tests the people in Judges to examine their obedience.
Theological contrast: In Exodus the people test God; in Judges 2 God tests the people to see if they will follow His way.
Contrasting parallel: In Exodus the question 'Is the Lord among us?' is used as doubt; in 1 Chronicles the same argument is used to affirm trust.
